analysis: Examined .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py (base lines 1-585 and head patch hunks @@ -5,14 +5,15, @@ -298,6 +299,83, @@ -350,6 +428,74, @@ -390,6 +536,25). The change is test-only CI tooling for the threat-review Bedrock scanner. It adds imports (SimpleNamespace, Scanner, ThreatContext). It adds tests for a 'workload' call policy: planned-call admission, an emergency ceiling of 500, a 16384 output-token cap, and read timeouts of 240s/600s with SDK retries disabled. It also tests that invalid policy, ceiling or token configs are rejected and cannot expand paid work. Two large synthetic scans exercise hierarchical integration and one repair. New status_body tests assert that incomplete final results require a human and are not reported as clean. None of these touch provider/coordinator code, the WebSocket contract (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), keys, prompts or caches in the threat model; no threat-model asset or assumption is affected. The tests assert fail-closed behavior: no fallback on a budget stop, and clean() returns false for incomplete scans. The implementation modules (threat_review/bedrock.py, budget_scan.py, budget_runner.py, merge_policy.py) are not in this batch. Whether they actually enforce the ceiling, token cap and clearance gating as the tests expect is unverified here and is a CI-billing/gating concern outside the provider threat model's scope. No regression identified.
